title: Training Loops, Epochs & Batches — Keep the Accelerator Fed
key_insight: Data loaders can prepare batches in worker processes, pin transfer-friendly memory, and prefetch the next batch while the current one runs.
body:
## Keep the Accelerator Fed

A fast GPU waits idle because the CPU loads and prepares each batch too slowly. The model is not the bottleneck.

Data loaders can prepare batches in worker processes, pin transfer-friendly memory, and prefetch the next batch while the current one runs.

Measure examples per second and data-wait time. Larger batches improve hardware use until memory fills, but they also change optimization behavior.
common_mistakes: An epoch is one single number inside a feature.
Validation should secretly train the model.
Larger batches always fit in memory and always improve accuracy.
mini_exercise: Sketch the situation in “Keep the Accelerator Fed” as three labeled steps, then explain what changes at each step.
real_world_usage: Correct loop structure keeps data, gradients, evaluation, and progress measurements in the right order.
